title: Sum of Average 2
statementMd:
## Problem Statement

You are given a length-$N$ sequence of positive integers $A=(A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_N)$.

Find the minimum possible value of $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\left\lfloor\frac{A_i+A_{i+1}}2 \right\rfloor$ after rearranging $A$ in any order.

You are given $T$ test cases; solve each of them.

## Constraints

- $1\le T\le 10^5$
- $2\le N\le 2\times 10^5$
- $1\le A_i\le 10^9$
- The sum of $N$ over all test cases is at most $2\times 10^5$.
- All input values are integers.

## Input

The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

```
T
\text{case}_1
\text{case}_2
\vdots
\text{case}_T
```

Each test case is given in the following format:

```
N
A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N
```

## Output

Output the answers for the test cases in order, separated by newlines.

samples.note:
Consider the first test case.

For example, rearranging $A$ as $(3,2,1,4)$ gives $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\left\lfloor\frac{A_i+A_{i+1}}2 \right\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac52\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac32\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac52\right\rfloor=5$.

No matter how $A$ is rearranged, the value of $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\left\lfloor\frac{A_i+A_{i+1}}2 \right\rfloor$ is at least $5$, so the answer is $5$.
